stem: A client in an acute-care hospital is identified as colonized with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) and is being transferred to another facility. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Maintain Isolation and Contact Precautions and ensure the receiving facility is notified of the client's CRE colonization status
options.B: Discontinue transmission-based precautions because colonized clients cannot transmit CRE
options.C: Use Airborne Precautions because CRE is primarily spread by airborne droplet nuclei
options.D: Withhold the CRE information from the receiving facility unless the client develops a symptomatic infection

rationale: Current CDC CRE guidance recommends Isolation and Contact Precautions in acute-care settings and emphasizes communication of CRE infection or colonization status during interfacility transfer. Colonized clients can contribute to transmission, and CRE spreads mainly through contact with contaminated hands, wounds, stool, equipment, or the healthcare environment rather than the airborne route.
educational_objective: Apply current CRE infection-control and interfacility communication practices to prevent transmission.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_locator: Infection prevention and control — Isolation and Contact Precautions in acute care; Safe patient transfers — notify receiving facility about CRE infection or colonization
source_claim_supported: Acute-care CRE colonization requires targeted contact-based precautions and communication during transfer.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission precautions and safe transfer communication
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — CRE containment
correction_summary: Updated terminology to Enterobacterales, specified acute-care setting, removed treatment-option overclaim, and converted recall into a transfer/infection-control decision aligned with current CDC guidance.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Acute-care isolation/contact precautions and transfer notification are explicit.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; status must be communicated during transfer.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A combines correct precautions and communication.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked infection vs colonization, acute care vs nursing-home precautions, taxonomy and interfacility communication; no unresolved conflict.
